Every known version of a filing

Source: R/api-cvm-versions.R
cvm_versions.Rd

An issuer may file the same document more than once: a DFP or ITR re-filed to fix a figure, a scale, a note. cvm_fetch() returns the current version of each document, as the CVM's yearly files do. cvm_versions() returns every version the package knows of, the current one included, so the figures of a filing can be followed from one version to the next. The signature mirrors the part of cvm_fetch() that identifies the documents (dataset, table, cnpj, ticker, year, basis) and takes none of its row filters: reading, from/to and as_of select rows of the current reading and are refused here.

Only the tables that keep a single filing per document (those whose schema declares keep_latest_version: the DFP, ITR and FRE detail tables, among others) have a version history. Asking for another table, such as a dataset's submissao index or the CAD register, aborts: those already return every row the CVM publishes. The list of tables is in the section Arguments by table of cvm_fetch().

Usage

cvm_versions(
  dataset,
  table,
  cnpj = NULL,
  ticker = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  basis = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  on_error = "abort",
  validate = "strict",
  ...
)

Arguments

dataset

Short dataset id (e.g. "cad", "dfp").

table

Snake-case table name (e.g. "companhias", "bpa"). For tables published in individual and consolidated variants, table is the concept name and basis selects the variant(s).

cnpj

Optional character vector of issuer CNPJs, with or without punctuation ("00.000.000/0001-91" or "00000000000191"). Only CNPJs are accepted: a CVM code or a company name aborts with cvmdata_error_input. NULL (default) keeps every issuer. A CNPJ absent from the table yields zero rows for it, silently.

ticker

Optional character vector of B3 trading codes ("PETR4", "BBAS3"). Each ticker is resolved to its issuer CNPJ through fca/valor_mobiliario (read from the same source) and then filtered like cnpj; the two arguments combine. The lookup reads every yearly FCA file that carries trading codes (2018 onwards), so the code of a company that has since left the exchange still resolves, for any year. A ticker absent from every file aborts with cvmdata_error_input; so does a ticker that maps to more than one issuer (pass cnpj instead).

year

Integer vector of years whose documents to return, as the CVM publishes them (one file per year). NULL (default) uses the latest available year.

basis

Individual ("ind"), consolidated ("con") or both (c("ind", "con")) financial statements. Required for tables that publish the two variants (bpa, bpp, dre, dra, dfc_md, dfc_mi, dmpl, dva): there is no default, because many issuers file only individual statements. Those tables always carry a basis column in the result, even when a single value was requested. Must be NULL for every other table; passing it aborts.

source

One of "mirror" (parquet via DuckDB) or "cvm" (CVM Open Data Portal). NULL (default) resolves to the active backend via cvm_source_get().

on_error

One of "abort" (default), "warn" or "silent". Controls behaviour on HTTP failures when several yearly files are read (year with more than one element, or a from/to window spanning several years). With "warn", the failed years are skipped and a cvmdata_warn_partial_failure warning lists them; with "silent", they are skipped silently; with "abort", the first failure aborts the call. Total failure always aborts.

validate

One of "strict" (default), "warn" or "skip". Controls schema validation strictness at parse time.

...

Reserved; any extra argument aborts. reading, from/to and as_of are refused by name.

Value

A cvm_tbl (a tibble subclass) with the columns of the table, basis for the tables published in individual and consolidated variants, and the five version columns described above. Empty when the issuers have no filing in the period.

Where the versions come from

The two backends know different parts of the history.

  • source = "mirror" (the default) reads, for every partition of the table, the current asset cvm_fetch() reads plus the history asset the ETL keeps next to it with the superseded filings, dated. The history holds the filings the mirror saw being replaced from 2026-10 on and, for the DFP and ITR statements, the ones recovered from the CVM's filing system (RAD) back to 2010; history_source says which ("mirror" or "rad").

  • source = "cvm" reads the CVM's yearly CSV without collapsing it to the current filing. That file keeps only the versions the CVM still publishes, usually the current one alone, and carries no supersession date, so superseded_at, id_doc and motivo_reapresentacao are NA there; the call says so once. The complete history is on the mirror.

Columns

The columns of the table, year and basis as cvm_fetch() returns them, then five version columns:

  • superseded_at: Date the version stopped being the current one (the receipt date of the version that replaced it); NA for the current version.

  • superseded_by_versao: the versao of the filing that replaced it; NA for the current version.

  • history_source: "current" for the rows of the current version, "mirror" or "rad" for a superseded version on the mirror, "cvm" for a superseded version still in the CVM's yearly file.

  • id_doc: the CVM document id of the superseded filing, when the history knows it.

  • motivo_reapresentacao: the reason the issuer gave for the re-filing, as the CVM publishes it, when known.

Rows are ordered by issuer, reference date and versao. versao is not a key on its own: the CVM index carries two filings under the same VERSAO for some documents.

See also

Other fetchers: cvm_fetch()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# Petrobras filed its consolidated 2023 income statement twice;
# version 1 was superseded on 2024-03-25 and net income (account
# 3.11, exercise row) is the same in both.
petr <- cvm_versions(
  "dfp",
  "dre",
  ticker = "PETR4",
  year = 2023,
  basis = "con"
)
petr[
  petr$cd_conta == "3.11" & petr$ordem_exerc == "ÚLTIMO",
  c("versao", "superseded_at", "superseded_by_versao", "vl_conta")
]

# Braskem filed it three times: version 1 in R$ units by mistake
# (a loss of R$ 4.5 million), version 2 "to reflect the R$ thousand
# scale" (R$ 4.89 billion) and version 3.
brkm <- cvm_versions(
  "dfp",
  "dre",
  cnpj = "42.150.391/0001-70",
  year = 2023,
  basis = "con"
)
unique(brkm[, c("versao", "superseded_at", "motivo_reapresentacao")])
}
